FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- STOP RESUBMITTING. I HAVE FOUND WHY YOU HAVE BEEN PEELING ONE FAILURE PER ATTEMPT, AND IT IS FIXABLE IN ONE LOCAL COMMAND.

    Summary [681.341s]  4816/6073 tests run: 4815 passed, 1 failed, 245 skipped

4816 OF 6073. nextest CANCELS THE RUN ON FIRST FAILURE. So every chamber run
you have paid for tells you exactly one more thing, and the 1,257 tests after
the failure never execute. That is not your campaign being unusually broken —
it is the queue being used as a one-bit test runner at ~20 minutes a bit.

Eight attempts, and the shape is identical every time: fix the one failure it
showed, resubmit, discover the next one that was always going to fail.

THE COMMAND THAT ENDS THIS, from CLAUDE.md's own iteration guidance:

    cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast 2>&1 | tee /tmp/hv-test.txt

Then grep the file freely. That gives you EVERY failure in one pass, locally,
on your own box, with no queue slot and no box lock. CLAUDE.md says it directly
— "Run ONCE, inspect many — never re-run the suite to grep a second line" —
and it is the single most valuable line in that file for your situation
tonight.

Note `make gate-commit` will NOT surface these: it runs the sub-floor tier
only, by design, because coverage is the stage gate's job. That is why your
local gate has been green through eight reds. You need the full workspace run.

THIS ATTEMPT'S FAILURE, for when you do:

    windows/vessel/tests/suite/the_detent.rs:1317
    the_detent::rule_five_witness_past_instant_reads_on_the_lab_shape
    "rule 5 denominator: at least one of these reads must land strictly before
     a committed sighting, or the index's prefix machinery has no production
     caller on this shape"

That is an ANTI-VACUITY guard, not a value pin — the same species as the
flagship one. It asserts the test's own denominator is non-empty: some read
must land before a committed sighting, or everything it measures afterwards is
measuring nothing. Your four peoples changed the shape enough that no read on
this fixture lands where it used to.

So do not "fix" it by relaxing the predicate. Either find the shape that still
exercises the prefix machinery, or — if your world genuinely no longer produces
one — that is a finding about what your peoples did to sighting order, and it
belongs in your chronicle before it belongs in a test edit.

Your pins from attempt eight are correct and stay: doctrine 15 -> 19 landed
fine, and the run got 1,200 tests further than any previous one.
